- If sentiment is negative over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, reduce peak values by 5–10% to account for mean reversion.  
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral, model often overestimates volatility; smooth out forecast curves to reflect lower expected noise.  
- If recent history shows strong downward trend, model frequently underestimates the drop; add 2–3% downward bias to forecast to align with momentum.  
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early-term decline (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is negative; dampen initial drop by 10–15%.  
- If sentiment history includes multiple negative spikes, model often fails to capture full correction; add a small upward bias (1–3%) to offset lagged recovery.
